review.summary: Mercedes lead the championship with 630 points after 19 rounds, having taken 12 wins and 24 podiums. Antonelli tops both the drivers' standings and the team's tally on 380 points, while Russell sits fourth with 250. In Mexico City Antonelli completed a podium from fourth on the grid for 15 points, and Russell scored eight more from sixth.
review.lastRace: Antonelli finished third from fourth on the grid to take a podium and 15 points in Mexico City, while Russell dropped from second to sixth for 8 points.

review.summary: Ferrari are second with 504 points after 19 rounds and 13 podiums from two wins. Hamilton leads the pair on 259 points in third of the drivers' championship, narrowly ahead of Leclerc on 245 in fifth. In Mexico City Hamilton took a podium from pole for 18 points, while Leclerc scored 12 from fourth.
review.lastRace: Hamilton finished second from pole position to claim a podium and 18 points in Mexico City, while Leclerc added 12 more from fourth after starting third.

review.summary: Red Bull are third with 382 points after 19 rounds and 13 podiums from three wins. Verstappen leads comfortably on 261 points in second of the standings, well clear of Hadjar on 107 in eighth, with Lawson ninth on 83. In Mexico City Verstappen took victory from fifth on the grid for 25 points, and Hadjar scored two more from ninth.
review.lastRace: Verstappen won from fifth on the grid to take 25 points in Mexico City, while Hadjar finished ninth after starting seventh for 2 points.

review.summary: McLaren are fourth with 365 points after 19 rounds and seven podiums from two wins. Norris leads the pair on 221 points in sixth of the drivers' championship, ahead of Piastri on 144 in seventh. In Mexico City Norris scored 10 points from fifth, while Piastri finished thirteenth after starting twelfth without points.
review.lastRace: Norris finished fifth from sixth on the grid to take 10 points in Mexico City, while Piastri dropped to thirteenth for no points after starting twelfth.

review.summary: RB F1 Team are fifth with 108 points after 19 rounds but have taken no wins or podiums. Lindblad leads on 38 points in eleventh of the standings, well ahead of Tsunoda on a single point in twentieth. In Mexico City Lawson scored six points from a climb to seventh, while Lindblad retired without points.
review.lastRace: Lawson climbed from 22nd on the grid to seventh for 6 points in Mexico City, while Lindblad retired without points after starting eighth.

review.summary: Alpine are sixth with 69 points after 19 rounds and no wins or podiums. Gasly leads the pair on 42 points in tenth of the standings, ahead of Colapinto on 27 in twelfth. In Mexico City both drivers finished without points: Colapinto thirteenth after starting eleventh, and Gasly seventeenth from ninth.
review.lastRace: Neither driver scored in Mexico City; Colapinto finished thirteenth after starting eleventh and Gasly seventeenth from ninth.

review.summary: Haas are seventh with 31 points after 19 rounds but have taken no wins or podiums. Bearman leads on 23 points in thirteenth of the standings, ahead of Ocon on 7 in sixteenth, and Hirakawa on a single point in twenty-first. In Mexico City Hirakawa scored the team's lone point by finishing tenth from eighteenth on the grid, while Bearman retired without points after starting fourteenth.
review.lastRace: Hirakawa finished tenth from eighteenth on the grid to take Haas's lone point in Mexico City, while Bearman retired without points after starting fourteenth.

review.summary: Audi are eighth with 27 points after 19 rounds and no wins or podiums. Bortoleto narrowly leads the pair on 14 points in fourteenth of the standings, just ahead of Hülkenberg on 13 in fifteenth. In Mexico City Bortoleto scored 4 points from eighth, while Hülkenberg finished fourteenth after starting tenth without points.
review.lastRace: Bortoleto finished eighth from thirteenth on the grid to take 4 points in Mexico City, while Hülkenberg dropped to fourteenth for no points after starting tenth.

review.summary: Williams are ninth with 12 points after 19 rounds but have no wins or podiums. Sainz leads the pair on 7 points in eighteenth of the standings, ahead of Albon on 5 in nineteenth. In Mexico City both drivers finished without points: Albon eleventh after starting sixteenth, and Sainz twelfth from fifteenth.
review.lastRace: Neither driver scored in Mexico City; Albon finished eleventh after starting sixteenth and Sainz twelfth from fifteenth.

review.summary: Aston Martin are tenth with just 7 points after 19 rounds and no wins or podiums. Alonso leads on 7 points in seventeenth of the standings, while Stroll sits last on zero points in twenty-second. In Mexico City both drivers retired without points — Alonso from seventeenth and Stroll from nineteenth.
review.lastRace: Both Aston Martin cars retired in Mexico City without points, Stroll from nineteenth and Alonso from seventeenth on the grid.

review.summary: Cadillac are bottom with zero points after 19 rounds and no wins or podiums. Both drivers sit on zero — Bottas twenty-third and Pérez twenty-fourth in the standings. In Mexico City Pérez finished sixteenth from twentieth on the grid without points, while Bottas retired without points after starting twenty-first.
review.lastRace: Pérez finished sixteenth from twentieth on the grid for no points in Mexico City, while Bottas retired without points after starting twenty-first.

review.summary: Ducati lead the championship after 18 rounds, with eight wins and fifteen podiums. Their riders are well spread across the top: Marc Marquez tops the standings on 399 points ahead of Fabio Di Giannantonio in sixth on 265, Alex Marquez eighth on 197 and Francesco Bagnaia ninth on 173, with Franco Morbidelli and others trailing clear.
review.lastRace: Marc Marquez won the Grand Prix of Malaysia for 25 points, with Alex Marquez third on 16 and Fabio Di Giannantonio eighth on 8. Franco Morbidelli took tenth for six, Francesco Bagnaia thirteenth for three and Iker Lecuona fifteenth for one.

review.summary: Aprilia sit second after 18 rounds with eight wins and thirty-one podiums. Jorge Martin is their strongest rider, second on 355 points, just behind the leader, while Marco Bezzecchi follows closely in third on 332. Ai Ogura is fifth on 278 and Raul Fernandez seventh on 236, giving Aprilia a deep points haul spread across five riders.
review.lastRace: At the Grand Prix of Malaysia, Ai Ogura finished fourth to take thirteen points, with Marco Bezzecchi sixth for ten more. Both riders scored comfortably inside the top six.

review.summary: KTM are third after 18 rounds with two wins and eight podiums. Pedro Acosta is their standout, fourth on 295 points and well clear of the rest, while Enea Bastianini tenth on 134 and Brad Binder twelfth on 118 hold a solid middle order. Maverick Viñales, Pol Espargaro and Jonas Folger trail far down the standings.
review.lastRace: Pedro Acosta took second at the Grand Prix of Malaysia for twenty points, with Enea Bastianini fifth for eleven and Brad Binder ninth for seven. Maverick Viñales completed the scorers, fourteenth for one point.

review.summary: Honda are fourth after 18 rounds with no wins and no podiums. Their best rider is Luca Marini, thirteenth on 117 points, ahead of Diogo Moreira fifteenth on 78 and Johann Zarco seventeenth on 51. Joan Mir eighteenth on 33 and the rest trail well clear, leaving Honda without a single win or podium this season.
review.lastRace: At the Grand Prix of Malaysia, Luca Marini finished seventh for nine points, their only scorer. Johann Zarco, Diogo Moreira and Joan Mir all failed to finish, going unclassified with no points on the board.

review.summary: Yamaha are fifth after 18 rounds with no wins and no podiums.
